title: Mushroom Scientists
statementMd:
As you very well know, the whole Universe traditionally uses three-dimensional Cartesian system of coordinates. In this system each point corresponds to three real coordinates $(*x*, *y*, *z*)$. In this coordinate system, the distance between the center of the Universe and the point is calculated by the following formula: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/22cac0bdb059f63ba2e16e3aabb38be91c9a9e6a.png). Mushroom scientists that work for the Great Mushroom King think that the Universe isn't exactly right and the distance from the center of the Universe to a point equals $*x*^{*a*}·*y*^{*b*}·*z*^{*c*}$.

To test the metric of mushroom scientists, the usual scientists offered them a task: find such $*x*, *y*, *z*$ $(0 ≤ *x*, *y*, *z*; *x* + *y* + *z* ≤ *S*)$, that the distance between the center of the Universe and the point $(*x*, *y*, *z*)$ is maximum possible in the metric of mushroom scientists. The mushroom scientists aren't good at maths, so they commissioned you to do the task.

Note that in this problem, it is considered that $0^{0} = 1$.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $*S*$ $(1 ≤ *S* ≤ 10^{3})$ — the maximum sum of coordinates of the sought point.

The second line contains three space-separated integers $*a*$, $*b*$, $*c*$ $(0 ≤ *a*, *b*, *c* ≤ 10^{3})$ — the numbers that describe the metric of mushroom scientists.

## Output

Print three real numbers — the coordinates of the point that reaches maximum value in the metrics of mushroom scientists. If there are multiple answers, print any of them that meets the limitations.

A natural logarithm of distance from the center of the Universe to the given point in the metric of mushroom scientists shouldn't differ from the natural logarithm of the maximum distance by more than $10^{ - 6}$. We think that $*ln*(0) =  - ∞$.
statementZhMd:
众所周知，整个宇宙传统上使用三维笛卡尔坐标系。在这个坐标系中，每个点都对应三个实数坐标 $(*x*, *y*, *z*)$。在该坐标系中，宇宙中心与某点之间的距离由以下公式计算：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/22cac0bdb059f63ba2e16e3aabb38be91c9a9e6a.png)。为伟大蘑菇王工作的蘑菇科学家认为，宇宙并不完全正确，宇宙中心到某点的距离应当等于 $*x*^{*a*}·*y*^{*b*}·*z*^{*c*}$。

为了检验蘑菇科学家的度量方式，普通科学家给他们提出了一个任务：找出满足 $*x*, *y*, *z*$ $(0 ≤ *x*, *y*, *z*; *x* + *y* + *z* ≤ *S*)$ 的点，使得在蘑菇科学家的度量方式下，宇宙中心与点 $(*x*, *y*, *z*)$ 之间的距离尽可能大。蘑菇科学家不擅长数学，因此他们委托你来完成这个任务。

注意，在本题中，规定 $0^{0} = 1$。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*S*$ $(1 ≤ *S* ≤ 10^{3})$——所求点的坐标之和的最大值。

第二行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 $*a*, *b*, *c*$ $(0 ≤ *a*, *b*, *c* ≤ 10^{3})$——描述蘑菇科学家度量方式的参数。

## 输出格式

输出三个实数——使蘑菇科学家度量方式下的距离达到最大值的点的坐标。如果有多个答案，输出其中任意一个满足限制的答案即可。

给定点在蘑菇科学家度量方式下到宇宙中心的距离的自然对数，与最大距离的自然对数之差的绝对值不应超过 $10^{ - 6}$。我们认为 $*ln*(0) =  - ∞$。
